content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident fired for service=frontend-eu-west-1 - alert=LB_Targets_Unhealthy (high error rate from ALB to target group)
pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident #INC-2024-7893 auto-escalated to on-call. Trigger: 503s and TLS handshake errors reported from edge. Priority: P1. Acknowledged by oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: Acked. I'm on it. Getting initial scope now.
netops: Seeing elevated 502/503 rates from the ALB in eu-west-1 to pool frontend-v2. CloudWatch shows target unhealthy count spiking around 02:12 UTC.
alice: Any customer-facing impact? Support reported a few 502/503s from API requests in EU. No large-scale 5xx surge yet in US.
bob: Quick check: curl logs from edge to backend show TLS handshake resets. Running:
```
$ curl -v https://frontend-eu.redwood.example/status
* Connected to frontend-eu.redwood.example (10.2.3.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLS handshake failed: unexpected message
* Closing connection 0
``` 
carol: Huh — TLS unexpected message suggests SNI/cipher mismatch or the backend process resetting connection. NetTCP shows RST from 10.2.3.45:443 -> 10.2.4.10:53312
netops: Also seeing Route53 changes in the last 24h for canary hostnames; TTLs are low (60s) but some replica weights were shifted during a rollout earlier today.
oncall-sre: Hypothesis: a partial rollout of frontend-v2 with incompatible TLS config caused a subset of targets to fail handshake, ALB marked those unhealthy, causing increased errors. Plan: 1) remove bad targets from target group 2) shift traffic to healthy nodes 3) rollback rollout if needed.
sre-lead: Agreed. NetOps, please confirm how quickly we can remove targets and whether we need a maintenance window for weights.
netops: We can set target group health-check to drain and adjust weights in Route53 weighted record immediately. Doing removal of 3/8 targets now. ETA ~60s.
oncall-sre: Doing ALB target deregistration (command):
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234
``` 
alice: I'll update customers in status page: small subset of EU traffic may see 503s, engineering investigating. Posting message on status.redwood.example now.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by oncall-sre, timer started for escalation policy. Auto-notify if not resolved in 30m.
bob: After removing the three failing targets, ALB error rate dropped by ~65% in the graph. Health checks returning 200 for remaining targets.
carol: Checking certs on failing hosts: looks like a deprecated OpenSSL build served TLS 1.0 fallback, and our ALB expects TLS1.2+ with modern ciphers. That would explain the handshake failures.
oncall-sre: Can we hot-patch the nodes or remove them from rotation permanently? Is there a risk of further rollouts including these hosts?
netops: The problematic hosts were part of the canary batch from today's deploy; patching would require rolling the instance image. For immediate mitigation, we'll mark them out of the target group and pin traffic to v1 instances.
sre-lead: Do it. Also start a rollback of the canary rollout to avoid further unhealthy hosts.
oncall-sre: Initiating rollback of today's canary rollout to stop further propagation. Rolling back via deploy-control:
```
deploy-control rollback --app frontend --to-version 2024-07-12-rc1
``` 
alice: Status page updated with "Mitigation in progress: rollback initiated; partial impact in EU region". Adding note to customers: "If you continue to see errors, please retry after 30s." :white_check_mark:
bob: Observability note: I pushed a temporary dashboard showing per-target TLS handshake failures and ALB target health. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/target-health (internal)
carol: For post-incident follow-up: need to add TLS compatibility checks to canary gating and prevent instances with old OpenSSL from joining the canary pool.
netops: Also saw DNS churn earlier — a Route53 weight shift at 01:58 that assigned 20% to the canary pool. Will add a guard to prevent weight changes during deploy windows.
oncall-sre: PagerDuty handoff: I will remain primary for 30 minutes to watch metrics, then hand off to netops for remediation tasks. @pagerduty please note handoff.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: handoff recorded. New assignee: netops. Next escalation in 30m if not resolved.
alice: Customer support sig-alert: we had 12 direct tickets in EU in the last 20m. Marking severity as degraded for EU customers. Posting an incident banner.
carol: Actions tracked: (1) Remove bad targets (done) (2) Rollback canary (in progress) (3) Patch image pipeline to enforce OpenSSL version (todo) (4) Postmortem owner: carol.
netops: Rollback completed. All new canary instances removed. ALB error rate back to baseline ~3m after rollback. Health checks stable.
oncall-sre: Monitoring 10m window. If no regressions, we'll resolve the incident and start RCA.
alice: Updated status: "Mitigated — traffic restored for EU; engineers continue remediation. ETA for full resolution: 4h (patching and deploy validation)."
sre-lead: Good containment. Please add runbook entry to prevent similar rollouts and add TLS checks to CI. Assign follow-up tickets.
carol: I'll own the postmortem and create the RFC for canary gating. Will include timeline and required deploy checks.
oncall-sre: Closing remarks before resolve: confirm customers are stable, PD acknowledged, rollback successful. If any new 5xx spikes, re-open the page.
incident-bot: Incident resolved automatically by PagerDuty after acknowledgment expiry without further alerts. Resolution note: rollback and target removal mitigated TLS handshake failures in eu-west-1.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: incident #INC-2024-7893 marked resolved. Please proceed with postmortem and follow-ups.
alice: Filing status update and tagging customers contacted. Thanks team :thumbsup:
carol: Postmortem slack doc will be posted in #postmortems and linked here when ready.

[reactions: oncall-sre :white_check_mark:, netops :hammer_and_wrench:, alice :memo: ]
